boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all seven frozen records in Jackson’s Valley Campaign. Preserve per-engagement dates, including Princeton’s May 15–17 interval and separate Cross Keys/Port Republic dates. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 9,500 total (US 3,500; CS 6,000). The live NPS field reads 9500 total (US 3500; CS 6000;).
claims.rationale: Source field only. Formations, engaged troops and changing concentrations do not establish matched opening populations. Live zeros are not measured absence; shared provenance is not independent corroboration.

claims.value: NPS describes assaults over bottomland and a flanking movement at the Coaling.
claims.rationale: Attributed local geography and maneuver, not a verified terrain coefficient or reconstruction of every approach.

citations.quote: a flanking column turned the Union left flank at the Coaling.

claims.value: Allan says a defective footbridge delayed the crossing and that Jackson attacked with Winder before the remainder had arrived.
claims.rationale: An approach constraint and changing troop population, not an opening readiness score. Later concentration cannot be treated as strength available at the first attack.

citations.locator: p.158 (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: The foot-bridge was defective, and a good deal of time was lost in getting the troops over.

citations.locator: p.158 (OCR page markers; not checked against print)
citations.quote: without Avaiting for the remainder of his forces, ordered an attack upon Tyler as soon as Winder had reached the vicinity of the Federals.

claims.rationale: No original reconnaissance, order or message chain was inspected to establish contemporary knowledge. Surprise in a summary does not independently establish what each commander knew.

claims.value: NPS describes Jackson concentrating against Tyler and Carroll’s isolated brigades.
claims.rationale: Immediate objective and opponent, not proof of complete destruction or measured campaign contribution.

citations.quote: against the isolated brigades of Tyler and Carroll

claims.value: NPS identifies Tyler as commanding the brigades of Shields’s division opposed to Jackson.
claims.rationale: Local command, parent division and army command are distinct; Shields’s name does not establish his presence or equal outcome credit.

citations.quote: of Shields's division, Brig. Gen. Erastus Tyler commanding.

claims.value: NPS reports Confederate troops moving from Cross Keys to Port Republic and burning the North River Bridge behind them.
claims.rationale: The related June 8 and June 9 engagements remain separate frozen records with changing populations; shared troops are not independent army observations and campaign success is not an extra victory credited to both.

citations.quote: Confederate forces at Cross Keys marched to join Jackson at Port Republic burning the North River Bridge behind them.

claims.value: The frozen result remains Confederate victory.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,818 total (US 1,002; CS 816). The live NPS field reads 1800 total (US 1000; CS 800;).
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Original orders, returns, casualty reconciliation, contemporary message chains and precise command clocks remain deferred after the bounded pass. No whole-book, facsimile or map verification is claimed.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Allan is one interested retrospective history where used. Embedded reports are not additional independently inspected families. Princeton retains only the frozen NPS/CWSAC family.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
